title: SpecJudgeVerdict
description: Output of the Spec Judge over a full set of specs for one decomposition. Two parts: per-spec grading against the spec rubric, and set-level coherence (do the specs fit together and cover the outcome). The judge never edits specs; it only reports.

round.description: Which spec-judge round this is. The orchestrator escalates to a human after max_rounds.

summary_for_human.description: What a reviewer at Gate 2 should know in 60 seconds. Written even on pass.

criteria.description: One entry per rubric criterion in rubrics/spec.md. Scores are independent; the rubric names the criteria.

score.description: 0 = fails, 1 = partially, 2 = meets, 3 = exemplary. Rubric defines the anchors.

evidence.description: Quote or reference to the spec text that justifies the score.

interface_mismatches.description: Spec A produces an interface that Spec B consumes with a different shape or name.

overlaps.description: Two specs change the same behaviour or paths without a declared dependency.

gaps.description: Something the outcome or decomposition requires that no spec delivers.

ordering_problems.description: Declared dependencies that are wrong, missing, or cyclic.

goal_coverage.description: For each success metric in the outcome: which acceptance criteria, across all specs, actually move it. This is the judge's answer to 'does this set achieve the goal'.

location.description: spec_id and section or AC id, or 'set' for cross-spec issues.

suggested_resolution.description: Advice to the spec writer. Not a rewrite; the judge does not author specs.
